newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire expects steady copper, cobalt output in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Zaire expects steady copper, cobalt output in 1997.

text.p: Zaire's state-run mining company Gecamines expects production in 1997 to remain at the same level as in 1996, officials in the capital of the southern mining province of Shaba said.
Gecamines estimates for 1996 are 42,000 tonnes of copper and 4,200 tonnes of cobalt.
"In 1997 production will be at around the same level as this year as our survival plan continues," technical director Yumba Monga told Reuters in the southern mining city of Lubumbashi.
"We are now working on a new five-year plan which will begin in 1998."

Output has fallen from highs in the mid-1980s, when copper production stood at 470,000 tonnes a year and cobalt at 17,000. Low points were reached in 1993, with cobalt output of 2,000 tonnes, and 1994, when copper sank to 30,000 tonnes.

A recovery plan targeting cobalt prevented the collapse of the company after output was hit by political and ethnic violence, a delay on major projects, ageing equipment and a desperate lack of finance.

"In future I don't think the accent will be so much on cobalt as it has been for our survival plan because other projects in other parts of the world may make it less attractive than it has been recently," said Yumba.
The political temperature in Shaba has fallen significantly since 1993, when as many as 10,000 of Gecamines' 30,000 workers were driven out of the region by those of Shaban origin.
"We have had to retrain a lot of staff to do different jobs, and that is now proving effective," said Yumba.
In 1995 and 1996 only a few days were lost to strikes, while the employment of a South African security firm had reduced losses from theft of products and equipment.
Yumba said he did not think that the rebellion which had erupted in eastern Zaire in recent weeks posed a direct threat to the mines.
A number of foreign mining companies have expressed interest in partnerships with Gecamines to exploit reserves.
